absent: Encoding produced for combined CPU and node values and width of each field.
Layout and indexing of the global descriptor table beyond CPU node and double fault entries.
Implementation of the flexible return user entry point and of paranoid entry handling.
Guest communication block setup and secure encrypted virtualization mapping conditions.
System call, APIC, translation, debug register, platform UV and fixed mapping initialization internals.
Idle routine selection, mitigation selection, EFI virtual mode entry and memory encryption details.
Performance microcode check, vendor microcode check and early NUMA node resolution.
Extended state size computation beyond legacy, guest default handling and supervisor feature set definition.
Exact fault vectors, gate descriptor layout and system vector set semantics.
Thread flag handling for needing floating point load and register lock protocol.

findings.text: Per CPU exception handling bringup prepares the current processor for faults. It records CPU and node identity for the paranoid path, programs interrupt stacks unless flexible return mode is active, prepares IO permission state, installs and loads the task state descriptor, prepares the confidential guest communication block, enables segment base management before any fault when supported, then selects flexible return initialization plus stack levels or loading of the current table depending on mode and boot versus secondary role.

General per CPU initialization fixes the NUMA node from early firmware data when unset, clears virtualization related control bits on 64 bit or when relevant features exist, and on 64 bit resets segment state, thread local entries, system call entry, filesystem bases, APIC and posted interrupt state. It then attaches the initial address space with a held reference, checks that no user space is active, initializes translation state with lazy handling, points the ring transition stack at the entry trampoline, loads the local table, initializes debug registers, prepares double fault state and applies platform and fixed mapping setup.

Boot processor finalization runs once during early start. It identifies the boot processor, chooses the idle routine, publishes threading counts, prints processor information on non symmetric builds, selects mitigations and refreshes threading related workaround and APIC state, enforces a minimum processor level and adjusts the machine name on 32 bit, initializes floating point system and per CPU state before alternatives and EFI virtual mode entry, copies boot capabilities into the per CPU record, patches alternatives, establishes user pointer limits and small page policy on 64 bit or checks floating point bugs on 32 bit, then initializes memory encryption after late time setup.

Early interrupt descriptor replacement runs during initialization and chooses between flexible return exception setup and installation of the early page fault table based on whether flexible return mode is enabled.

Floating point subsystem bringup proceeds in ordered phases of early generic detection, per CPU enablement, legacy user state creation with MXCSR discovery, legacy size selection, extended state sizing and architecture task size derivation. Per CPU bringup enables operating system support for save restore extensions, normalizes task switched and emulation controls, clears pending legacy state, enables extended save support and programs feature masks and dynamic gate state before allowing kernel mode floating point.

Flexible return exception enablement initializes the stack segment to the kernel data selector, programs the configuration control with red zone reservation, zero interrupt level and user entry point, clears level to vector mapping, resynchronizes the level zero stack pointer from its per CPU cache after offline online cycles, clears higher level pointers, sets the control enable bit, disables further descriptor table use and disables legacy fast 32 bit system call capabilities.

Flexible return stack configuration assigns dedicated levels to debug, nonmaskable, machine check and double fault vectors while user faults remain on level zero, then loads the corresponding stack pointers for debug, nonmaskable and double fault from per CPU interrupt stack tops.

Interrupt descriptor helpers provide invalidation by loading an empty descriptor, loading of the current table under disabled interrupts, early page fault table installation from a static vector list and generic table construction that initializes each gate, writes it at its vector index and optionally records the vector as a system vector.

Local descriptor table loading for an address space observes the table pointer once, tolerates concurrent replacement protected by inter processor notification, validates the isolation slot and programs the processor either through an isolation alias or directly from table entries, clearing the table when absent or when validation fails.

Capability handling refreshes the maximum CPUID function, copies boot capabilities including synthetic entries, then reads hardware leaves. After microcode activity it repeats performance and vendor checks, re-reads capabilities and warns that feature changes may not take effect and recommends early loading or firmware update when the mask differs.

User floating point state initialization prepares compacted format metadata then selects extended save defaults or legacy defaults. Kernel floating point exit restores permission with a warning check and releases the register lock when interrupts are enabled. Extended CPU state setup programs operating system save support, dynamic gate state, user feature mask and supervisor plus independent masks when supervisor save is present.

Double fault per CPU setup points the double fault task state stack at the top of the per CPU entry area stack and installs the matching global descriptor entry, compensating for static per CPU initialization limits. Posted interrupt setup programs a fixed notification vector and a destination derived from the per CPU APIC identifier with distinct handling for extended and legacy modes.

Threading update refreshes speculative execution workaround state and APIC broadcast decisions. Legacy floating point bug detection runs a short division and multiply sequence under kernel floating point protection and records the division bug with a warning when the computed error is nonzero. Hardware without CPUID support is probed by clearing task switched and emulation controls, issuing legacy init plus status reads and checking signature values to force or clear the floating point capability.

Interrupt stack tables are programmed only when flexible return mode is off. When the mode is on, the descriptor table is invalidated and must not be used further. The boot processor enables flexible return during early boot while secondaries enable it during per CPU exception bringup, but all processors program flexible return stack levels when the mode is active.

When segment base read write support is enabled, its control bit is set and the corresponding hardware capability is advertised before any exception can occur, because secondary processors start after global patching and early fault handling may already rely on patched base accesses.

Virtual mode extension controls are cleared on 64 bit unconditionally and on 32 bit when virtual mode, timestamp or debugging features are present. Floating point generic bringup sets operating system support bits for save restore extensions only when boot features indicate them, clears task switched and emulation bits, sets emulation when no floating point unit exists and issues legacy initialization.

Extended state per CPU setup does nothing without save support or configured features. Otherwise it enables operating system save support, synchronizes dynamic gate state from the initial state when supported, programs user features into the user mask control and programs supervisor plus independent features into the supervisor control when supervisor save is present. The supervisor mask is the kernel maximum intersected with supported supervisor set, and the independent mask excludes branch records unless the architecture branch feature is enabled.

CPU and node identity encoding is written to the timestamp auxiliary control only when timestamp counter read with processor identifier capabilities exist, and is always mirrored into a global descriptor entry that is readable from user mode as a present 32 bit non system segment with limit fields carrying the encoding.

In descriptor table mode the task state interrupt stack entries for double fault, nonmaskable, debug, machine check and virtualization communication exceptions are each set to the top of the corresponding per CPU stack. The virtualization entry is only mapped when the relevant secure encrypted virtualization extension is active. An alternate build provides an empty operation.

The task state IO bitmap base is set to an invalid offset. When IO permission support is built, the cached maximum and sequence are zeroed, the bitmap is filled to deny all ports and the trailing entry beyond the full permission map is set to all denied as required by hardware.

Generic table construction walks a caller supplied vector list, initializes a temporary gate, writes it at the listed vector and when system mode is requested records each vector in the system vector set. Early page fault setup uses this mechanism with the early fault list in system mode.

Legacy floating point size selection prefers software state when no floating point unit is present, extended save state with floating point plus SSE features when save restore extensions exist, otherwise legacy register state with floating point only. The chosen size is published to kernel maximum and default, user maximum and default and guest default configurations.

MXCSR feature mask discovery probes hardware with extended save when available, substitutes a default allowing all except denormals are zero when hardware reports zero and intersects the global mask with the discovered value.

Architecture task size equals base task structure plus floating point container minus static register union plus dynamically computed default register size, with a build time assertion that the register state ends the floating point container with proper alignment.

Early floating point detection marks the thread as needing state load, and on processors without CPUID support probes hardware to force or clear the floating point capability. Absence of both hardware support and emulation halts the boot processor after an emergency message.
Current descriptor table loading requires interrupts disabled, enforced by an assertion before loading the table descriptor.

Local descriptor table loading uses a single volatile read coordinated with inter processor notification after table replacement, with lifetime guaranteed until all active processors handle the notification. Conversion to read copy update would still require interrupts disabled to avoid racing a newer load, and callers must ensure the observed pointer remains safe even if replaced before return.

Kernel floating point exit warns when permission state is unexpected, marks permission allowed and releases the floating point register lock only when interrupts are enabled. One build warns once on violation while the other only checks validity at build time.

The CPU node descriptor in the global table is a data segment whose limit fields together carry the combined CPU and node encoding, configured as read only expand down accessed, user privilege, non system, present and 32 bit, written through the per CPU writable table at the CPU node index with a data descriptor type.

The task state interrupt stack array provides dedicated slots for double fault, nonmaskable, debug, machine check and virtualization communication vectors, each holding a virtual address of the corresponding per CPU stack top. IO permission state adds a base offset plus cached maximum, sequence, bitmap and full permission map.

Floating point register state has three legacy variants of software, extended save with control plus MXCSR and legacy with control, status, tag and offset words. Extended save adds a header carrying feature and compacted format metadata selected according to save restore support.

Flexible return controls consist of configuration, level to vector mapping and four stack pointers, with levels encoded as two bit fields positioned by vector number. The local descriptor isolation alias layout is a fixed base plus per slot stride times slot index.

The boot interrupt path moves from early table through replacement to steady state. Early page fault table is installed when flexible return is off and flexible return is enabled when on, then per CPU logic selects flexible return stack levels or current table load. Once flexible return is enabled, any descriptor table use is erroneous.

Floating point bringup orders early detection, per CPU enablement, user initial state plus MXCSR discovery, legacy sizing, extended sizing and task size publication. Per CPU extended setup is skipped when save support or maximum features are absent.

Capability state starts from boot capabilities, is refreshed per processor from hardware leaves and is rechecked after microcode loading. A mismatch leaves behavior unchanged but triggers warnings recommending early loading.

If the stack segment is not initialized to the kernel data selector before enabling flexible return, a kernel event delivered before first user entry can later cause a general protection fault on return after a context switch changes the segment.
After an offline online cycle the flexible return level zero stack pointer cache can diverge from hardware and must be resynchronized. Failure leaves exception delivery on a stale stack.
Continued descriptor table use after flexible return enablement is a bug. Invalidation loads an empty table to make such use fault.
When compacted extended save format is enabled, the compacted indicator must be set in the header alongside the feature mask or restore with supervisor state triggers a general protection fault.
A local descriptor table slot beyond the first two indicates either an unmapped table or a bogus mapping. The handler warns once, clears the table and returns without programming hardware.

Double fault stack linkage cannot be resolved statically for per CPU variables pointing within per CPU space and must be patched at runtime before installing the descriptor. Missing patch leaves the task state with an invalid stack.

Enabling patched base accesses before setting their control bit, performing direct memory access before bounce buffer decryption marking or late microcode changes to capabilities can cause early faults, incorrect decryption or silently ineffective features.

The CPU node segment uses fixed numeric attributes for read only expand down accessed type, user privilege level, non system class, present and 32 bit operation, with identity encoding split across two limit fields.

Default floating point controls are a specific extended control word with default MXCSR, and legacy words for control, status, tag and offset. Zero hardware MXCSR mask substitutes a default with all features except denormals are zero.

Flexible return stack level for a vector is encoded by shifting the level by twice the vector number. Configuration reserves red zone space, fixes interrupt level zero and points at the user entry symbol, while debug, nonmaskable, machine check and double fault vectors use dedicated higher levels.

The isolation alias for a local descriptor slot is computed as a fixed base plus slot index times a fixed stride. Posted interrupt destination placement differs between extended and legacy APIC modes, with direct use in extended mode and shifted placement otherwise.
